DILG BAGONG PIUPINAS Republic Of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, west Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph on-G OPINION NO. 52 MAR 2 5 2025 MR. GLICERIO M. MONTON, JR. Jabonga, Agusan del Norte Dear Mr. Monton: This pertains to your communication seeking this Departments legal opinion on the following: I. Whether you should be considered entitled to all back salaries and other benefits with no deduction against your accumulated credits for your detention on account of you being arrested; and 2. Whether Section 60, 62 and 64 ofthe Local Government Code is applicable to your case. In your letter, you mentioned that you were the former Municipal Vice Mayor of Jabonga, Agusan del Norte, with your last term supposedly ending on June 30, 2022. However, on November 28, 2018, you were arrested and detained due to criminal cases filed against you. On July 26, 2023, you were acquitted of these charges. When you received your back salaries, the computation showed that all your accumulated leave credits were exhausted, leaving nothing for your terminal leave benefit. Additionally, your back salaries were only computed up to April 30, 2021. This computation was based on a legal opinion issued by the Civil Service Commission, which was later concurred with by the Commission on Audit. Hence, your request for legal opinion. As to your first query, relevant is the opinion and recommendation of the Civil Service Commission (CSC) in their letter dated September 1, 2023 which states: Please be informed that we maintain our previous stand that Mr. Monton, Jr. is considered on automatic leave of absence from the day he was detained on 28 November 2018 up to his last day in elective office on 30 June 2022. The determination whether his leave of absence is with or without pay depends on the sufficiency of his eared leave credits to cover for his absence. We ended our opinion with a suggestion to the LGU-Jabonga to consider the said factors in the computation of his leave credits and terminal leave benefit. However, as to the actual computation of the salaries and eamed leave credits of Mr. Monton, Jr., we advise you to closely coordinate with the concerned LGU in order to ascertain based on available "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. 8876-34-54

records whether or not (i) salaries are still due him for the period of Auqust 2019 to 30 June 2022. and (i) he still has leave balances from July 1998 to 28 November 2018 to support his claim for terminal leave pay. (Emphasis supplied) As to the applicability of Galzotel case, the CSC in their letter opined: As can be gleaned above, Ms. Galzote was considered on automatic leave of absence for the period of her detention, and she was adjudged to be paid with back wages and other benefits only from 19 October 1994, which was the date when she presented herself for resumption of duties after her acquittal but was refused by the City Govemment of Makati, up to the time that she was actually reinstated to her position. Thus, while we your predicaments, we find that the factual circumstances in the above-cited case are not applicable to the situation of Mr. Monton, Jr. insofar as the claim for back wages and other benefits is concemed. With that, we go back to our original proposition that the determination whether his automatic leave of absence is with or without pay depends on the sufficiency of his eamed leave credits to cover for such absence. We, therefore, reiterate our advice for you to coordinate with the LGU-Jabonga with respect to the actual computation of the salaries and terminal leave benefit that are still due to him, if any. Relatively, on July 6, 2023, the Commission on Audit (COA) wrote to the Mayor Napoleon M. Montero, M.D., of Jabonga, Agusan Del Norte, viz: As a result of our audit of Summary of Leave Credits and Leave Card for the leave benefit computation of the former vice-mayor, it was noted that he already incurred Leave of Absence Without Pay as of May 31, 2021. Thus, no balance left to be paid for his Terminal Leave Benefit, and he could only get his back salaries up to April 30, 2021. In response to your query, this Department agrees with the position of the two (2) Commission having the expertise in addressing your issue on backwages and terminal leave benefits. We agree with the CSC that the Galzote case is not applicable in your case. First, the RTC did not order your reinstatement and payment of backwages, hence, the discussion of the CSC is applicable. Second, you are an elective official whose term ended on June 30, 2022. Considering that you are not in agreement with the postulation of the CSC and COA, we recommend that you raise your issues before the courts of law. This Department does not have the jurisdiction to overtum the opinions of the said offices who have the expertise to discuss on the matter. 1 City Government of Makati vs. Civil Service Commission, G.R. No. 131392, February 6, 2002. 20f3

Regarding your second query, it is our opinion that Sections 60, 62, and 64 of the LGC are not applicable to your case. Section 60 of the LGC outlines the grounds for disciplinary action against elective local officials, while Section 62 provides the rules for issuing notices of hearing in administrative cases. Section 64, on the other hand, while it states that subsequent exoneration and reinstatement entitle the respondent official to full salary or compensation, including emoluments accruing during suspension, it is important to note that said provision applies only when the respondent official is preventively suspended due to an administrative complaint. In your case, your absence was not due to preventive suspension following an administrative complaint but rather due to your detention on account ofthe criminal charges. This opinion is based solely on our appreciation of the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and the attachments thereof. As caveat, however, this Office would defer to the opinion of higher or more competent authorities, or to any jurisprudence, if there be any. We hope we have addressed your concem accordingly. Very truly yours, By authority of the Secretary: ATTY. ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal, and Legislative Affairs cc: MARIA LOISELLA E. LUCINO, CESO IV Regional Director, DILG XIII- CARAGA Region Purok I-A, Brgy. Doongan, Butuan City 3 of 3
